decisions.reason: As a specialized two-component injection unit with meaningful support and manufacturing costs, two years of dedicated promotion followed by no later website presence suggests the market test has largely resolved negatively and the option is no longer worth carrying.

Like A, this resin injection unit is close to the firm's capabilities but costly enough that the lack of continuing visibility after the initial trial period points to insufficient realized demand to justify further commitment.

An automatic airless spray gun fits the firm's core coating business and can be supported through existing channels at relatively low incremental cost, so it is still worth keeping as a complementary option despite limited public evidence.
A manual airless spray gun is easier for rivals to match and, without continued visible traction after 2019, its strategic upside appears too limited to warrant keeping it on the market.

An air-assisted airless spray gun is closely aligned with the firm's established application technology and likely inexpensive to keep in the portfolio, preserving option value across varied industrial use cases.
The data logger was already downgraded from its own page to a mere mention by 2019, which is a strong signal that this option was deprioritized early and is unlikely to justify further resources.
